output_json.patch_notes: In extractArchive(), immediately after computing `final File file = new File(destination, entry.getName())`, each entry is validated with a new private helper `isInsideDestination(File file, File destination)`. The helper compares `file.getCanonicalPath()` against `destination.getCanonicalPath()`, allowing only paths equal to the destination or beginning with `destination + File.separator`. If validation fails (or canonicalization throws IOException, treated as unsafe), an ArchiveExtractionException is thrown before the directory-creation (mkdirs) and FileOutputStream write paths flagged in the alert (lines 518, 542-543, 547). This closes all three reported sink traces since they all flow from the same `file` object. The existing extractFiles() wrapper logs and swallows the ArchiveExtractionException, so a malicious archive is skipped rather than aborting the whole scan, preserving prior error-handling behavior. Legitimate nested-directory entries still extract normally because their canonical paths remain under the destination. Added regression test testZipSlipIsBlocked which crafts a zip with a `../PWNED` entry, invokes the real private extractFiles via reflection with an Engine whose accept() returns true, and asserts the escaped file is never created. Verified: the provided POV now exits 1 (was exit 0), and the ArchiveAnalyzerTest suite builds and passes.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The change only adds a rejection path for entries whose canonical location falls outside the extraction directory; benign entries (including legitimate subdirectories) are unaffected. Canonicalization can differ from raw paths on symlinked temp dirs, but since both destination and file are canonicalized consistently, normal extraction still resolves inside destination. If canonical resolution fails with IOException the entry is conservatively rejected, which could in rare filesystem-error cases skip a legitimate entry, but it will never permit a traversal write. No dependencies or public API changed.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-022) in ArchiveAnalyzer.extractArchive where archive entry names were used to build extraction targets via new File(destination, entry.getName()) without validating containment. Added a canonical-path containment check that rejects any entry resolving outside the destination directory before any directory creation or file write, and added a regression test.
